title: GAP Waiver Addenda Claim Service Standards and Time Limits
content:
The time limits below govern GAP Waiver Addenda claims. All six plans carry the same figures. Every period is counted in calendar days.

| Standard | Every plan |
|---|---|
| Claim must be reported within | 90 calendar days after the date of loss |
| Complete claim file must be received within | 90 calendar days after the primary insurer's settlement |
| Theft must remain unrecovered before the claim is decided | 30 calendar days |
| Claim is decided within | 30 calendar days after the complete claim file is received |
| Approved benefit is credited to the contract within | 10 calendar days after approval |
| Written denial stating its reason is mailed within | 10 calendar days after a denial |
| Claim withdrawn because the vehicle was repaired rather than declared a total loss | the addendum returns to active |

**A complete claim file contains:**

- the primary insurer's settlement letter;
- the primary insurer's valuation report;
- a police report, for a theft;
- a copy of the contract;
- the payment history.

### Questions the standards answer

- *Each clock starts on a different event. Which?* The reporting period starts on the date of loss. The document period starts on the primary insurer's settlement. The decision period starts when the complete file is received. The crediting period starts on approval, and the denial-notice period starts on the denial.
- *What happens to the addendum when a reported vehicle is repaired instead?* The claim is withdrawn and the addendum is active again.
